item.title: BinDex
item.description:
Over the years, I’ve accumulated so many random parts, cables, tools, and other things that it’s been impossible to keep track of them all. So much so that when I’ve started a project, I’ve reordered things I already had on hand because I didn’t remember I had them in the first place.

I explored existing inventory software (UnderMyRoof, HomeBox, and many other random iPad apps), but they all seemed like overkill and too complicated for what I needed. My idea was a simple, single-page web app backed by a SQLite database that could run as a Docker container on my NAS. I had existing Node.js scaffolding from previous projects that would work here, but why do it myself when I could have Codex one-shot it?

item.title: Receipt Printing Adventures
item.description:
This was a quick and fun little project that I cobbled together based on some similar projects I’d seen on Twitter.

The idea is simple: push a button, and a “daily summary” report prints out. It has the date, weather, upcoming rocket launches, stock info, and a daily fact and quote.

I also decided to add a second button that prints out a random picture of my girlfriend and me. (It seemed like a fun little Easter egg!)

item.title: Labels Made Easy
item.description: I work as a systems engineer at a big tech company, but back home my family is in the bakery business. In my spare time, I like to build things to help make the bakery more efficient and organized. By far, my biggest bakery project has been an order tracking system I like to call OrderMonger, but that’s a story for a different day. Today, I want to talk about the inventory labeling system I built from scratch in less than two weeks.

item.title: ESXi Cluster - Part 1
item.description:
A few months ago a friend of mine was offloading some old(er) 2U Supermicro Servers. I decided to grab a couple and turn them into a 2-node ESXi cluster!

Part 1 of this series will focus on specs, cabling, and IPMI configuration.
